The size is 1 << tile_count tiles of 1 << (tile_size + 6) texels, so 1024 tiles of 256 texels is tile_count=10, tile_size=2. Each water info texture texel covers 78.1 m (7812.5 uu). Depth color and shore foam come from this texture, so large texels flatten the shallow-to-deep transition and shore foam may never appear; use a smaller water zone (or several) rather than a higher resolution. If render_target_resolution_verified is false, this number is unconfirmed. A large zone can also make the renderer bias the ocean tile size, which only shows in the log (a LogWater warning); keep extent/2/tile_size below 256.

scheduled/generated does not mean the world reflects your new settings: PCG reuses cached output when settings are edited through reflection, because that does not invalidate the node's cached CRC (set_pcg_node_properties does).
